misconfigurations.scenario: EKS pods or worker nodes are overprovisioned for observed workload demand
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: CPU, memory, and network utilization over reviewed 14-, 30-, and 90-day windows, including a 40% safety margin, remains below requested pod resources or worker-node capacity.
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Right-size pod requests, limits, and worker-node capacity after reviewing workload seasonality, autoscaling behavior, disruption budgets, and peak demand.

misconfigurations.scenario: Amazon EKS clusters do not have GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection enabled
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: GuardDuty EKS Runtime Monitoring is not enabled with no threat detection for containerized workloads
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Enable GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection for EKS to monitor container runtime behavior and detect threats in Kubernetes environments
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Announced at re:Inforce 2025, GuardDuty now provides runtime threat detection for EKS clusters. This monitors container behavior, Kubernetes API calls, and pod-level network activity to detect threats like cryptocurrency mining, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. Without this protection, compromised containers can operate undetected.
misconfigurations.notes: AWS re:Inforce 2025: GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection for EKS announced

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS cluster API endpoint is publicly reachable from unrestricted CIDRs
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: endpointPublicAccess is enabled and publicAccessCidrs contains 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Restrict public endpoint CIDRs or migrate administrative access to a reviewed private endpoint path.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Unrestricted EKS API exposure increases control-plane attack surface. Access changes must preserve a validated administrative path.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS cluster private API endpoint is disabled while public access is enabled
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: endpointPrivateAccess is false and endpointPublicAccess is true
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Plan a reachable private administration path before enabling the private endpoint and restricting public access.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Private endpoint access reduces public control-plane exposure, but an unsafe transition can lock operators out.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS control-plane logging does not include every supported log type
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: One or more of api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, or scheduler logging is disabled
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Enable missing control-plane log types after reviewing CloudWatch retention and cost.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Incomplete logging limits incident response and operational diagnosis. Audit or authenticator gaps materially reduce security visibility.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS Kubernetes version is in extended support or approaching end of support
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: The current version support status or support dates indicate extended support or less than 90 days remaining
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Validate add-ons, APIs, node groups, workloads, and rollback capacity before planning a supported version upgrade.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Unsupported or aging Kubernetes versions lose fixes and can constrain safe upgrade paths.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS managed node group Kubernetes version is behind its cluster version
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: Managed node group minor version differs from the cluster minor version
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Review workload disruption budgets and available capacity before planning a node group upgrade.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Version skew can restrict support and complicate future cluster upgrades.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS managed node group uses an outdated EKS-optimized AMI release
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: A newer EKS-optimized AMI release is available for a managed AMI node group; custom AMIs are excluded
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Review launch template compatibility, PDBs, and spare capacity before planning the AMI update.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Outdated managed AMIs can miss security and runtime fixes. Custom AMIs require a separate provenance review.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS managed node group reports health issues
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Correlate the health issue with Kubernetes node conditions, workloads, events, PDBs, and capacity before changing the node group.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Managed node group health issues can reduce capacity or block safe deployments.

misconfigurations.scenario: EKS managed add-on reports a degraded or failed status
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: Managed add-on status is DEGRADED, CREATE_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, or DELETE_FAILED, or health issues are present
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Correlate add-on health with kube-system pods and events before planning an update or configuration change.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: A degraded networking, DNS, proxy, or storage add-on can affect broad portions of the cluster.

misconfigurations.scenario: A compatible default version update is available for an EKS managed add-on
misconfigurations.alert_criteria: The installed add-on version differs from the default compatible version returned for the cluster Kubernetes version
misconfigurations.recommendation_action: Review compatibility, configuration conflicts, workload health, and rollback steps before planning the add-on update.
misconfigurations.recommendation_description_detailed: Compatible add-on updates can include fixes, but an available update alone does not prove the installed add-on is unhealthy.
